No problem, here it is in plain terms.

Imagine a year group of students split into classes. The **micro** average pools every student's mark into one big list and divides once — so a class of fifty students pulls the number much harder than a class of five. The **macro** average instead works out each class's average mark first, then averages *those* class-averages together — so the five-student class counts exactly as much as the fifty-student one, no matter how few students it has.

That's exactly what's at stake in your eval. The agent set `bucket_average: macro` in the config. Your long-context bucket is probably small and hard — maybe only a few dozen examples compared to thousands of short-context ones. Under macro averaging, that small, hard bucket now pulls just as hard on the overall number as any other bucket, which means the final figure you see is a *different quantity* than the single accuracy number you had before — not the same measurement with more detail added, a genuinely different calculation.
